solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Speaks to God, we hear — appropriate words?

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the word is identified by pronunciation rather than spelling

parts.note: one who speaks to God prays

explanation.surface: A worshipper at prayer wonders which words are fitting to address to God.
explanation.walkthrough: PRAYS and PRAISE sound identical. The question mark flags that the definition is loose: words of praise are the words appropriate when speaking to God.
explanation.definitionFit: Hymns and prayers of worship consist largely of glorifying language, the fitting kind of speech to offer a deity.

clue.text: One won't fight agreement seeing condition is included

indicators.note: something included is held within something else, so these letters go inside the outer word

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to fight once a treaty is signed that includes a condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agreement' is split open so that the two short words sit between its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A conscientious objector who rejects war and violence on principle is exactly a person refusing to take up arms.

clue.text: Article on church in American valley in fall

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

parts.note: A is a common abbreviation for American
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A news story about a church standing in some American valley that took a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the article sits over the church, and that pair goes inside the American valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowslide is a sudden fall of snow and ice down a mountainside, so fall is a general term covering it.

clue.text: Country one leaves for period

indicators.note: whatever leaves is gone, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An emigrant departs their homeland for a stretch of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I from SPAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A span of time is a stretch or interval, a synonym for a length of duration.

clue.text: Picture, landscape, given turn in print?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a painting or photograph of a person
second meaning: page orientation; rotate a landscape page a quarter turn and it becomes the tall format

explanation.walkthrough: In printing, pages are set either landscape (wide) or portrait (tall); turning one through ninety degrees gives the other. The question mark flags this playful second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a painted likeness of a person and the upright page layout used in document printing settings.

clue.text: Lorry had broken down — dickens!

indicators.note: something broken down comes apart, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A driver exclaims in frustration when their truck breaks down on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dickens' is not the novelist: in 'what the dickens!' it is a euphemism for the devil, which is also what the old name Old Harry means.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old British euphemistic nicknames for Satan, used in exclamations of annoyance or surprise.

clue.text: Is part-time working help towards success in field?

indicators.note: working suggests being worked on or processed, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a part-time job helps a person get ahead in their career field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' suggests a line of work but means a sports field.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective morale and cooperation among players is an asset that helps a side win matches on the pitch.

clue.text: Part of rare, natural sporting venue

indicators.note: a part of some words is a fragment of them, so the answer lies within the letters that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A rare natural setting that doubles as a place for sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the letters through 'r-ARE, NA-tural', ignoring the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium or enclosed area where contests and games are staged for spectators.

clue.text: Papers in bank, comparatively neat

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: a tier is a bank or row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Documents kept in a bank are, relatively speaking, in good order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money, but here it is a row or layer, as in a bank of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative form of an adjective meaning orderly: more neat is more orderly.

clue.text: Capital of French — Louvre, highlight? Indeed, first of all

indicators.note: first of all asks for the opening letter of every word in the run

parts.note: the initials of the three words

explanation.surface: A visitor to Paris decides the Louvre is the highlight of the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of French' reads as Paris, but 'Capital' alone is the definition and 'of French' is a translation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city is the seat of government, and a seat of government is a capital.

clue.text: Cleaner promotion — ultimately risible travesty

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is kept

explanation.surface: A cleaner's promotion at work turns out to be laughable.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is an old British word for a woman paid to clean houses.
explanation.definitionFit: An absurd pretence or sham is a mockery of the real thing, just as a travesty is.

clue.text: No way out — change demanded, Mike no longer needed

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so these letters are rearranged
what is no longer needed is discarded, so that letter drops out

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Trapped with no exit, someone demands change now that Mike is surplus to requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M from DEMANDED and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A cul-de-sac or blind alley offers no exit, and figuratively a hopeless situation leading nowhere.

clue.text: Criticism of liquid carrier when son is missed out

indicators.note: anything missed out is omitted, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone is blamed over a drinks bottle once their son is left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the S out of FLASK.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh censure is informally called this, from the anti-aircraft fire that came under attack.

clue.text: Keep cash at building — and become this?

definitions.text: Keep cash at building — and become this?

indicators.note: building something assembles it from parts, so these letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: If you keep hoarding money and let it build up, you may end up a miser.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the anagram fodder describes the behaviour of the person it spells.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingy person who hoards money rather than spending it is exactly what the clue warns one might turn into.

clue.text: One particular day I will be entertained by sort of food ritual

definitions.note: noun here; the answer is also a noun meaning a system of rites

indicators.note: a guest entertained is hosted inside, so these letters go within another word

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday, one particular day of the week

explanation.surface: On one special day, someone joins in a food-based ritual as a guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertained' suggests hospitality, but it means held inside: the day and I go together into the breakfast food.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a prescribed set of formal rites, which is what a ritual is.

clue.text: To some extent becomes a creditor, worthy of respect

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only part of the following letters is used

parts.note: the letters span the three words

explanation.surface: Someone who lends money gains a measure of standing and respect.
explanation.walkthrough: Read through 'become-S A CRED-itor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something holy or hallowed is venerated and must be treated with reverence.

clue.text: Judge's supporter coming back — one term unfinished

indicators.note: something coming back travels the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a bra is a supporting garment

indicators.note: unfinished means lacking its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A judge's backer returns while one term of office is left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge’s' reads as possessive, but the ’s stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay. A supporter is a bra, a favourite crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone appointed to settle a dispute decides the outcome, as a judge does.

clue.text: Specialist notices changes, receiving award

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so the outer letters take the others inside
changes means alters, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An expert spots changes and is honoured with an award.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert in finance and markets is one kind of specialist; the definition is deliberately broad.

clue.text: Urgent move forward, extremely neat

parts.note: to stride is to step forward

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outer ends, so only those letters are kept

explanation.surface: An urgent instruction to step forward in a very tidy way, like a drill order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Urgent' here means loudly insistent rather than time-critical.
explanation.definitionFit: Demands or voices described this way are harsh and insistent, pressing their case forcefully and loudly.

clue.text: Like Burnham? On the contrary — source of right-wing article on navy

indicators.note: the contrary is the opposite way round, so the word runs backwards
a source is where something starts, so only the first letter is kept

explanation.surface: Is Burnham a right-winger? No, quite the reverse, despite a piece about the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy Burnham is the Mayor of Greater Manchester, dubbed the 'King of the North'. 'On the contrary' looks like a debating phrase, but it turns ON round.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnham is a politician strongly identified with England's north, so the adjective for that region describes him.

clue.text: What may help to recall internet feature often regularly circulating

parts.note: a meme is a joke or image spread online

indicators.note: circulating goes round, so the letters come back in the opposite order
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: its first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: An online feature that often goes round and helps people remember things.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the odd letters of 'often' and turn them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake or souvenir is kept to remind its owner of a person or event.

clue.text: Leading couples in kilts mostly, not clothing from East!

indicators.note: a leading couple is the front pair, so the first two letters of each word are kept

explanation.surface: Dancing couples at the front are mostly in kilts, not Eastern dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading couples' suggests dancers, but means the first two letters of each following word.
explanation.definitionFit: The loose wide-sleeved robe is traditional Japanese dress, a garment from the Far East.

clue.text: Oil riches not English unfortunately — millions

indicators.note: things that go unfortunately go wrong, so these letters end up jumbled
not means without, so that letter is left out

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Oil wealth fails to benefit England, which sadly loses millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil' suggests petroleum, but the answer is the consecrated oil used in church rites.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a mixture of olive oil and balsam blessed for anointing at baptism and confirmation.

clue.text: At core neglect part of church — drop in standards

indicators.note: the core is the centre, so only the middle letter is kept

parts.note: the apse is the rounded end of a church

explanation.surface: Neglect at the heart of the church has led to falling standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At core' looks like part of the surface's phrasing, but it asks for the middle letter of the seven-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip or decline from expected behaviour, a temporary failure to maintain quality.

clue.text: The man's tailor subtly introducing cut originally from the past

indicators.note: to introduce is to put in, so one letter goes inside the others
subtly suggests craft and alteration, so these letters are reworked
originally means at the origin, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A gentleman's tailor quietly brings in an old-fashioned cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor' looks like the craftsman but is the anagram fodder; C goes into the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything belonging to or concerning earlier times, rather than the present, is of history.

clue.text: One who might love Southern farm wagon

parts.note: a wain is an old word for a farm cart

explanation.surface: A Southern farm cart described as something one could fall for.
explanation.walkthrough: A wain is a large farm wagon, as in Constable's painting The Hay Wain.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetic or old usage, a young country lover or suitor courting a girl.

clue.text: Great number in country where World Cup is held

definitions.text: country where World Cup is held
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the nation staging a tournament

explanation.surface: Huge crowds turn up in the nation staging football's World Cup.
explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are joined by 'in', which reads naturally as part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a large crowd and also the nation that stages an international tournament for visiting teams.

clue.text: Sign of emotion? Be quick

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a drop from the eye when crying

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are pronounced differently: one rhymes with fear, the other with fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A teardrop shows sadness or joy, and to tear about means to race or hurry at speed.

clue.text: Fancy that is about parent with strong drink

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it, so these letters go around the rest

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that a mother has taken to hard liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' reads as ordinary phrasing, but 'that' alone gives IE, which here surrounds the rest; 'Fancy that' looks like the definition, but only 'Fancy' is.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to picture it in the mind or suppose it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Fruitless way — European anger

parts.note: St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A pointless route that stirs up European resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anger' reads as a noun but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren land or unproductive plants yield no fruit or offspring; figuratively it means unproductive.

clue.text: March maybe about leaders of old lingering in organisation resisting change

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: March is one example of a month

indicators.note: leaders go in front, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A protest march by veterans who linger in an institution that refuses to reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' suggests a demonstration, but 'maybe' shows it is an example of a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a large, uniform, rigid institution that is slow and unwilling to adapt.

clue.text: Particle — expert to explain finally

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter is used

explanation.surface: A physicist is called in to explain a particle at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Three short pieces run in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A positively charged subatomic constituent of every atomic nucleus is one such particle.
